answer:
Implement the simulation in legacy FEniCS (dolfin) using a vector-valued continuous Galerkin space of degree 1 for the displacement field.
Solve the 2D small-strain linear elasticity problem in the reduced plane-stress formulation, with the 2D Lamé parameters λ = E·ν/(1−ν²) and μ = E/(2·(1+ν)).
Use the material parameters E = 70e9 Pa, ν = 0.33, ρ = 2700 kg/m³, and g = 9.81 m/s².
Define the domain as a rectangular plate occupying (x, y) ∈ [0, 1] × [0, 0.5] with a circular hole of radius 0.1 m centred at (0.5, 0.25).
Generate the mesh with 64 cells per edge using a structured mesh with the hole removed.
Apply gravity as a body force f = (0, −ρ·g) added to the right-hand-side vector.
Impose a Dirichlet boundary condition u = 0 on the entire left edge x = 0.
Leave the boundary of the hole at (0.5, 0.25) traction-free.
Define the loaded arc as a circular arc of radius r_arc = 0.02 m, with its centre placed slightly inside the plate at (0.98, 0.25) so that the point (1.0, 0.25) lies on the mid-span of the arc.
Restrict the loaded arc to a small angular extent of 10°, spanning local polar angles from −5° to +5° (measured from the local +x axis of the arc-centred frame), so that the arc sits on the right edge of the plate around (1, 0.25).
Identify the arc cells via a MeshFunction that distinguishes the loaded arc from the rest of the right boundary, as well as from the left, top, bottom, and hole boundaries.
Apply the prescribed traction using the literal formula from the task: t_θ = M / (2·π·r_arc), with M = 800 N·m and r_arc = 0.02 m, giving the numerical magnitude t_θ ≈ 6366.2 N/m at every point of the arc.
At each loaded-arc node p, compute the outward normal of the plate boundary at p, rotate it by −90° (counter-clockwise rotation in the global xy plane) to obtain the tangential direction, and apply the traction vector +t_θ·t̂ on the outward normal side of that arc segment.
Add a code comment near the traction assignment explaining that the formula is taken literally from the task statement, even though the dimensional balance would require r_arc²; this caveat is informational only and does not change the value used.
Assemble the linear system with the bilinear form ∫ 2μ·ε(u):ε(v) + λ·tr(ε(u))·tr(ε(v)) dx (the reduced plane-stress form) and the load linear form ∫ f·v dx + ∫_arc t_θ (t̂·v) ds.
Solve the system with a direct linear solver (LU) provided by dolfin.
Post-process by computing the in-plane Cauchy stress σ = 2μ·ε(u) + λ·tr(ε(u))·I in plane-stress form using UFL projections onto a suitable discontinuous space, or equivalent component-wise projection.
Compute the von Mises stress as σ_vm = sqrt(σ_xx² + σ_yy² − σ_xx·σ_yy + 3·σ_xy²).
Export the displacement field and the von Mises stress field to VTK/PVD files (for example displacement.pvd and von_mises.pvd) using dolfin.File for inspection.
Print the minimum and maximum of the displacement magnitude and of the von Mises stress to stdout.
The script must be self-contained, runnable with legacy dolfin imports only (no dolfinx or UFL from dolfinx), and be the final deliverable for this task.
